ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r1.claim: The Prophet should persevere despite opponents, trust God, and seek patience through prayer and remembrance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r1.anchor: He will help him in every difficulty.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r2.claim: Disbelievers' real ailment is unwillingness to sacrifice immediate gains for the Hereafter; they fabricate objections despite its certainty, though recreating them is easy for God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p87/r2.anchor: The real ailment of the disbelievers is that they do not have the courage to sacrifice the immediate gains of this world

NAHHAS:v5p106/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p106/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p106/r7.claim: An implied 'from the night' completes the command to prostrate; night glorification is variously said abrogated, recommended, or specific to the Prophet.
NAHHAS:v5p106/r7.anchor: التقدير فاسجد له من الليل ( وسبحه ليلا طويلا ) قيل هو منسوخ بزوال فرض صلاة الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r3.claim: The instruction to prostrate at night refers specifically to night prayer, obligatory or voluntary, when the Prophet is free from public preaching.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الليل وقت تفرغ من بث الدعوة كما تقدم في قوله : { قم الليل إلا قليلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r4.claim: Because glorification is coordinated with night prostration, it refers here to voluntary devotion; tasbih also includes verbal praise, good speech, and reflection on God's attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r4.anchor: فتعين أن التسبيح التنفل . والتسبيح : التنزيه بالقول وبالاعتقاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r5.speaker: عبد الملك بن حبيب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r5.claim: He interprets ‘glorify Him’ here as voluntary night prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r5.anchor: وعن عبد الملك بن حبيب : و { سبحه } هنا صلاة التطوع في الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r6.claim: ‘A long night’ restricts the command to glorify: spend most of the night in worship, as in the instruction to stand except for a little.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r6.anchor: فتعين أن وصف الطول تقييد للأمر بالتسبيح ، أي سبحه أكثر الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r7.claim: They read morning and evening as the five prescribed prayers and their times, taking ‘evening’ to include noon; glorification then points to night prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وابن زيد : أن هاتين الآيتين إشارة إلى الصلوات الخمس وأوقاتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r8.claim: These instructions echo commands to glorify God, prostrate, remember Him, and persevere despite opponents' words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p405/r8.anchor: وهذه الآية جاءت على وفق قوله تعالى : { ولقد نعلم أنك يضيق صدرك بما يقولون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p294/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p294/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p294/r3.claim: Night prayer and glorification are also commanded, as in the instructions for night vigil in al-Isra and al-Muzzammil.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p294/r3.anchor: كقوله: {ومن الليل فتهجد به نافلة لك عسى أن يبعثك ربك مقاما محمودا}

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r3.claim: Worshipping at night means the sunset and late-night prayers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r4.claim: Long night glorification means voluntary night prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r4.anchor: يعني التطوع من الليل . قال ابن عباس وسفيان : كل تسبيح

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وسفيان
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r5.claim: Every occurrence of glorification in the Qur'an means prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p172/r5.anchor: كل تسبيح في القرآن هو صلاة

MUQATIL:76:23-26/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:76:23-26/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:76:23-26/r6.claim: The nighttime prayer means Isha before sleep and a long night of prayer; night vigil was obligatory for the Prophet, while tahajjud was an extra devotion for him.
MUQATIL:76:23-26/r6.anchor: { ومن الليل فاسجد له } يعني صلاة العشاء الآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r3.claim: Bowing at night refers to the sunset and late evening prayers; prolonged night glorification means voluntary night worship, a view Qurtubi finds sound.

QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r4.speaker: ابن حبيب
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r4.claim: Ibn Habib says prolonged night glorification means voluntary worship at night.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r4.anchor: قاله ابن جبيب. وقال ابن عباس وسفيان

QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وسفيان
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Sufyan say every occurrence of glorification in the Quran means prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وسفيان كل تسبيح في القرآن فهو صلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r6.claim: Alternatively, glorification may mean unrestricted remembrance, whether during prayer or outside it.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r6.anchor: هو الذكر المطلق سواء كان في الصلاة أو في غيرها

QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd and others say the command to glorify God through a long night was abrogated by the five prayers; other views call it recommended or specific to Muhammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:25-26/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وغيره: إن قوله: { وسبحه ليلا طويلا } منسوخ بالصلوات الخمس

RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r1.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r1.claim: One reading takes morning and evening remembrance as the five prayers: dawn, noon and afternoon, sunset and night; the long night glorification is night vigil.
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r1.anchor: البكرة هي صلاة الصبح والأصيل صلاة الظهر والعصر

RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r2.claim: Some held that night vigil was obligatory for the Prophet and later abrogated, reasoning that the repeated imperative expresses obligation.
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r2.anchor: كان ذلك من الواجبات على الرسول عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p228#2/r3.claim: Others held that the night vigil is voluntary and its ruling remains in force.

STUDYQURAN:76:25/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r1.speaker: Aj, JJ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r1.claim: The verses may enjoin naming God in the daily prayers; Aj also reads them as remembrance of God at every moment.
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r1.anchor: These verses enjoin mentioning the Name of God during the daily prayers

STUDYQURAN:76:25/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r2.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r2.claim: In context, the command counsels remembering God amid worldly tribulations; many Sufis take verse 25 as invoking God’s Supreme Name, Allāh.
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r2.anchor: many Sufis take v. 25 as an injunction to invoke the Supreme Divine Name, Allāh

STUDYQURAN:76:25/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r3.claim: Glorifying God at length by night enjoins voluntary night vigil and prayer, with related passages elsewhere and in 73:2, 6, and 20.
STUDYQURAN:76:25/r3.anchor: Glorify Him by night at length enjoins the supererogatory practice of night vigil and prayer

THALABI:v10p106/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p106/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p106/r2.claim: What lies behind people means what lies ahead of them, as in the cited verse; the heavy day is Judgment Day.
THALABI:v10p106/r2.anchor: ويذرون وراءهم أمامهم وقدامهم كقوله: وكان وراءهم ملك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r3.claim: Prostrating to God at night refers to the sunset and night prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r3.anchor: ومن الليل فاسجد له} يعني فصل له المغرب، والعشاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r4.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r4.claim: The long night glorification means voluntary prayer after the obligatory prayers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r4.anchor: يعني التطوع بعد المكتوبة، (وهو قول الكلبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r5.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r5.claim: He says night prayer was obligatory for Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r5.anchor: وقال عطاء: يريد أن صلاة الليل فريضة عليك يا محمد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r6.claim: He prefers voluntary prayer, since Muhammad was not required to pray the entire night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p60/r6.anchor: والقول هو الأول؛ لأنه كان لا يجب عليه أن يصلي جميع الليل

ELMALILI:76:25-31/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:25-31/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:25-31/r2.claim: “From the night” means some portion of the night; the command to prostrate explains remembrance as prayer, using a part (prostration) to mean the whole.
ELMALILI:76:25-31/r2.anchor: burada “fâ” ile فَٱسْجُدْ emri, وَٱذْكُرِ emrini de beyan ederek ondan da murad namaz olduğunu anlatır.

ELMALILI:76:25-31/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:25-31/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:25-31/r3.claim: The night portion denotes the evening and night prayers.
ELMALILI:76:25-31/r3.anchor: Gecenin bazı cüz’ü de akşam ve yatsı demek olur.

ELMALILI:76:25-31/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:76:25-31/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:76:25-31/r4.claim: Long night worship recalls the command to perform tahajjud and signals that the waiting for God’s decree may feel long; the Prophet and, indirectly, the community should stay awake in worship and preparation.
ELMALILI:76:25-31/r4.anchor: Peygamber’e teheccüdün vücûbuna tenbih olmakla beraber Rabbinin hükmü gelinceye kadar sabır emrolunan müddetin uzun bir gece gibi geleceğine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r1.claim: Morning and evening remembrance and worship strengthen the Prophet's devotion, resolve, and resistance to the polytheists' attacks.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r1.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in Allah’a derin saygı ve bağlılığının, irade ve azminin daha da güçlendirilmesinin ve müşriklerin çirkin saldırılarına karşı direncinin arttırılmasının amaçlandığı anlaşılmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r2.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r2.claim: One reported view takes remembrance as the five daily prayers: morning means dawn prayer, evening means noon and afternoon prayers, night prostration means sunset and night prayers, and extended night prayer is obligatory for the Prophet but recommended for his community.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r2.anchor: Râzî müfessirlerin bu âyetlerle ilgili görüşlerini üç maddede özetlemiştir: a) Bu âyetlerde beş vakit namaz emredilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r3.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r3.claim: A second reported view understands morning and evening remembrance as verbal glorification and belief in God's transcendence throughout day and night, rather than prayer alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r3.anchor: b) “Sabah akşam rabbin adını anmak”tan maksat namaz değil, sözle Allah’ı tesbih etmek ve O’nun noksan sıfatlardan münezzeh olduğuna inanmaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r4.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r4.claim: A third view includes all these forms of remembrance: obligatory prayer, voluntary prayer, supplication, and seeking forgiveness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r4.anchor: c) Allah’ı zikirden maksat bu söylenenlerin tamamıdır; farz olan beş vakit namaz, nâfile namazlarla dua ve istiğfarın hepsi bu zikre dahildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r5.claim: The author takes the verses broadly as stressing worship and devotion, especially prayer at parts of the night alongside glorification, supplication, repentance, and seeking forgiveness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:76:25/r5.anchor: Bize göre bu âyetlerde –beş vakit namaz da dahil olmak üzere– genel olarak ibadetin, özellikle gecenin belli vakitlerinde namaz kılmak

TAB-FULL:v23p574/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p574/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p574/r2.claim: The command is to pray at night and glorify God for a long time, meaning most of the night, as in the instruction to stand for all but a little of the night.
TAB-FULL:v23p574/r2.anchor: فسبحه ليلا طويلا، يعني: أكثر الليل

TAB-FULL:v23p574/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p574/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p574/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the verse as prayer and glorification.
TAB-FULL:v23p574/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ومن الليل فاسجد له وسبحه ليلا طويلا} [الإنسان: 26] يعني: الصلاة والتسبيح

BURSEVI:v10p214/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p214/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p214/r2.claim: Prostrating to God for part of the night may refer to the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers.
BURSEVI:v10p214/r2.anchor: وفي بعض اليل فصل له ولعله صلاة المغرب والعشاء

BURSEVI:v10p214/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p214/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p214/r3.claim: Putting the time phrase first emphasizes night prayer because its greater effort and sincerity away from display merit special attention; the most difficult, sincere deeds are best.
BURSEVI:v10p214/r3.anchor: وتقديم الظرف للاهتمام لما في صلاة الليل من مزيد كلفة وخلوص

BURSEVI:v10p214/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p214/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p214/r4.claim: The ف adds force as though the instruction were conditional: whatever may happen, prostrate to Him.
BURSEVI:v10p214/r4.anchor: ثم الفاء لإفادة معنى الشرط كأنه قال مهما يكن من شيء فاسجد له

BURSEVI:v10p214/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p214/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v10p214/r5.claim: The Najmiyya reading makes prostration the annihilation of the self, bowing the annihilation of attributes, and standing the annihilation of actions, as the devotee worships through the night of nature and dusk of human embodiment.
BURSEVI:v10p214/r5.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : واعبد ربك المطلق حق العبودية بالفناء فيه

BURSEVI:v10p214/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p214/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p214/r6.claim: The command means performing the night vigil, which was obligatory for the Prophet during a long portion of the night—two thirds, half, or one third.
BURSEVI:v10p214/r6.anchor: أي صل صلاة التهجد لأنه كان واجبا عليه في طائفة طويلة من الليل ثلثيه أو نصفه أو ثلثه

BURSEVI:v10p214/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p214/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p214/r7.claim: Calling the vigil “glorification” and placing its time phrase after the verb indicate that it does not have the rank of the preceding instruction.
BURSEVI:v10p214/r7.anchor: وفي التعبير في التهجد بالتسبيح وتأخير ظرفه دلالة على إنه ليس في مرتبة ما قبله

BURSEVI:v10p214/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p214/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p214/r8.claim: ليلا is an adverb and طويلا its adjective; “long” does not distinguish it from a short night, since shorter night prayer is also covered, but signals prolonging the worship.

QASHANI:76:26-28/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:76:26-28/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:76:26-28/r1.claim: Night marks the station of self or heart after annihilation, when one returns to creation for religious guidance; calling others requires the heart's veil and the self's presence.
QASHANI:76:26-28/r1.anchor: وخصص مقام النفس أو القلب حال البقاء بعد الفناء

QASHANI:76:26-28/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:76:26-28/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:76:26-28/r2.claim: Prostration is annihilation: seeing the self subsist through God and humanity perish, so one exists by Him rather than oneself, without duality, ego, or residue.
QASHANI:76:26-28/r2.anchor: سجود الفناء برؤية بقاء نفسك بالحق وفناء البشرية بالكلية فتكون موجودا به لا بها

QASHANI:76:26-28/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:76:26-28/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:76:26-28/r3.claim: The long night signifies abiding eternally in that station.
QASHANI:76:26-28/r3.anchor: بقاء دائما أبديا ما دمت في ذلك المقام

ITQAN:v2p497/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p497/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p497/r9.claim: Lām can carry the sense of ʿalā, 'on' or 'against', as in falling on chins, lying on one's side, and the curse being upon people.
ITQAN:v2p497/r9.anchor: وعلى نحو ﴿ ويخرون للأذقان ﴾ ﴿ دعانا لجنبه ﴾

ITQAN:v3p98/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.claim: The reverse figure names a part for the whole: 'face' means God's essence or the person facing, body-wide states are expressed by faces or hands, and prayer's standing, reciting, bowing, or prostrating can stand for the whole prayer.
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.anchor: عبر بالوجوه عن جميع الأجساد لأن التنعم والنصب حاصل بكلها

SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r1.claim: The verse refutes some rhetoricians' claim that combining ح and ه makes a word ineloquent; the cited criticism of such letter sequences does not fit this verse.
SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r1.anchor: فيه دليل على عدم ما قال بعض أهل علم المعاني والبيان: إن الجمع بين الحاء والهاء مثلا يخرج الكلمة عن فصاحتها

SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r2.claim: The alleged defect in Abu Tammam's line comes from repeating the same word, unlike the verse, which has no repetition.
SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r2.anchor: ويمكن أن يفرق بين ما أنشدوه وبين الآية الكريمة بأن التكرار في البيت هو المخرج له عن الفصاحة بخلاف الآية الكريمة فإنه لا تكرار فيها

SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r3.speaker: أبو تمام
SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r3.claim: Abu Tammam's cited wordplay repeats أمدحه and لمته, illustrating the criticized poetic construction.
SAMIN-DURR:76:26/r3.anchor: البيت لأبي تمام. ويمكن أن يفرق بين ما أنشدوه وبين الآية الكريمة

ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n24/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n24/r1.claim: Asad glosses the night devotion as extending to every time one is awake.
ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n24/r1.anchor: I.e., at all times of wakefulness.

ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n25/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n25/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n25/r1.claim: Asad presents the night devotion as consolation whenever unhappiness presses in and one's surroundings seem dark.
ASAD-NOTES:76:23#n25/r1.anchor: I.e., "whenever unhappiness oppresses thee and all seems dark around thee".

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r1.claim: Fronting the night phrase highlights the hardship of night worship and the stature of prostration, whose great reward suits its burden.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r1.anchor: لماذا قدّم الجار والمجرور على الفعل؟ لأن التهجد شاق على النفس فقدّم الليل بما يقابل الشدة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r2.speaker: النحاة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r2.claim: One grammatical account treats the fa as the answer to an implied condition: whatever the circumstances, prostrate to God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r2.anchor: قال النحاة أن الفاء قد تكون إما جواب شرط مقدّر يعني مهما كان الأمر فاسجد له

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r3.speaker: قسم آخر
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r3.claim: Another group treats the fa as extra, serving emphasis.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r3.anchor: وقسم آخر يقول أن الفاء زائدة للتوكيد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r4.claim: Whether conditional or extra, the fa emphasizes prostration and signals its importance and exalted status.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r4.anchor: وفي كلتا الحالتين يكون التوكيد للسجود والدلالة على أهميته وعظمته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r5.claim: The preceding waw and fronted phrase preserve the emphasis on prostration; saying first and prostrate to Him at night would lose that force.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p351/r5.anchor: وجاءت الواو قبلها أيضاً (ومن الليل فاسجد له) ولا يصح أن نقول (واسجد له من الليل) لأنها تفوت أهمية السجود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p352/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p352/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p352/r1.claim: Al-Muzzammil's early command puts night after the verb in the ordinary order; al-Insan later fronts it as the mission's burden grows and night worship becomes harder.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p352/r1.anchor: هذا الأمر في سورة المزمل جاء في أوائل الرسالة ثم لمّا اشتد الأمر أصبح فيه مشقة ويحتاج إلى صبر كما في سورة الإنسان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p352/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p352/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p352/r2.claim: The form tabtil is an intensive verbal noun, like tajrih from jarraha; the command develops from gradual worship to abundant worship.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p352/r2.anchor: وتبتيل مصدر الفعل بتّل وهو دلالة على التكثير مثل جرّح تجريح وتجرّع

NASHR:v1p218/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218/r1.claim: A voiced, strong articulation is especially important for the letter under discussion when vowelless before certain voiceless letters, lest it weaken and merge with shin; the excerpt also stresses this when doubled.
NASHR:v1p218/r1.anchor: وإذا سكنت وأتى بعدها بعض الحروف المهموسة كان الاحتراز بجهرها وشدتها أبلغ نحو: اجتمعوا، واجتنبوا

NASHR:v1p218/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218/r2.claim: The throat letter ḥāʾ must be clearly articulated before a matching or nearby letter, especially while vowelless; assimilating it or changing the hāʾ in wa-sabbihhu into ḥāʾ is unanimously impermissible.
NASHR:v1p218/r2.anchor: والحاء تجب العناية بإظهارها إذا وقع بعدها مجانسها، أو مقاربها، لا سيما إذا سكنت نحو: فاصفح عنهم، وسبحه

NASHR:v1p218/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218/r3.claim: Some speakers turn the hāʾ of wa-sabbihhu into ḥāʾ because hāʾ is weak and ḥāʾ draws it into a doubled sound; this pronunciation is unanimously forbidden.
NASHR:v1p218/r3.anchor: وكذلك يقلبون الهاء في " وسبحه " حاء لضعف الهاء وقوة الحاء فتجذبها فينطقون بحاء مشددة

NASHR:v1p218/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218/r4.claim: Keep ḥāʾ thin beside an emphatic letter, especially when emphatic letters flank it, to prevent it from becoming emphatic.
NASHR:v1p218/r4.anchor: كذلك يجب الاعتناء بترقيقها إذا جاورها حرف الاستعلاء نحو: أحطت، و (الحق) ، فإن اكتنفها حرفان كان ذلك أوجب نحو: حصحص

NASHR:v1p218/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218/r5.claim: Khāʾ and the other emphatic letters must be emphatic; fatha gives the strongest emphasis, followed by ḍamma and then kasra, as Ibn al-Tahhan classifies them.
NASHR:v1p218/r5.anchor: قال ابن الطحان الأندلسي في تجويده: المفخمات على ثلاثة أضرب

NASHR:v1p218/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218/r6.claim: A dāl that substitutes for tāʾ must be articulated distinctly so the tongue does not revert to its original letter.
NASHR:v1p218/r6.anchor: والدال: فإذا كانت بدلا من تاء وجب بيانها لئلا يميل اللسان بها إلى أصلها نحو: مزدجر، وتزدري

NASHR:v1p218/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p218/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p218/r7.claim: Articulate vowelless dhāl clearly before nūn and preserve its thin, open quality near emphatics, lest it become ẓāʾ; some Nabateans pronounce it as dāl and some non-Arabs as zāy.
NASHR:v1p218/r7.anchor: والذال: يعتنى بإظهارها إذا سكنت وأتى بعدها نون نحو: فنبذناه، وإذ نتقنا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r1.claim: Some of the night is devoted to prayer; prostration names the whole prayer, understood as the sunset and night prayers, with night prayer specially emphasized for its greater effort and sincerity.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r1.anchor: أي بعضه فاسجد فصل له عز وجل على أن السجود مجاز عن الصلاة بذكر الجزء وإرادة الكل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r2.claim: Tasbīḥ originally means declaring God free of imperfection, and can denote verbal or bodily worship generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r2.anchor: وأصل التسبيح التنزيه ويطلق على مطلق العبادة القولية والفعلية

ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd and others held that the night worship was once obligatory, then abrogated; only the five prayers are obligatory now.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن زيد وغيره أن ذلك كان فرضا ونسخ فلا فرض اليوم إلا الخمس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r4.speaker: قوم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r4.claim: Some say the command remains binding specifically for the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r4.anchor: وقال قوم هو محكم في شأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r5.speaker: آخرون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r5.claim: Others consider the command still in force generally, but as a recommendation.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون هو كذلك مطلقا على وجه الندب

ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r6.claim: Alusi questions the inference that the delayed time phrase and the word tasbīḥ prove this is not obligatory, as the preceding command is.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r6.anchor: وفي تأخير الظرف قبل دلالة على أنه ليس بفرض كالذي قبله وكذا في التعبير عنه بالتسبيح وفيه نظر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r7.claim: Al-Tibi reads the command as following the order to resist sinners and endure their hostility: devote all day and night to prayer and as much other worship as possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p166#2/r7.anchor: وقال الطيبي الأقرب من حيث النظم أنه تعالى لما نهى حبيبه عن إطاعة الآثم والكفور وحثه على الصبر على اذاهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:76:26-27/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:26-27/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:26-27/r1.claim: The command is to pray to God during part of the night, perhaps the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers; the temporal phrase comes first because night prayer entails greater effort and sincerity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:26-27/r1.anchor: وبعض الليل فصل له تعالى، ولعل المراد به صلاة المغرب والعشاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:76:26-27/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:26-27/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:26-27/r2.claim: He should perform night vigil for a substantial portion of the night.
BAYDAWI-FULL:76:26-27/r2.anchor: وتهجد له طائفة طويلة من الليل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r1.claim: A portion of the night is for worship, with the rest left for sleep and rest.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r2.claim: Here prostrating means praying Maghrib and Isha; mentioning prostration highlights the prayer's most excellent act and marks night as a time of submission.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r2.anchor: أي فصل له صلاتي المغرب والعشاء , وذكرهما بالسجود تنبيها على أنه أفضل الصلاة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r3.claim: Placing the time phrase first emphasizes night prayer's extra difficulty, sincerity, and merit: fewer sensory distractions make it less exposed to showing off and deepen humility and delight in worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r3.anchor: وتقديم الظرف لما في صلاة الليل من مزيد الكلفة والخلوص ومزيد الفضيلة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r4.claim: Glorifying God for a long night means tahajjud; the duration may be half the night, more, or less.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r4.anchor: أي بالتهجد { ليلا طويلا * } نصفه أو أكثر منه أو أقل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r5.claim: It is called glorification because struggling to rise and overcoming sleep recall God's majesty and transcendence; abandoning beloved rest signals profound love for God.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p276#2/r5.anchor: ولعله سماه تسبيحا لأن مكابدة القيام فيه وغلبة النوم تذكر بما لله من العظمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r8.claim: He is directed to continue preaching and remembering God in varied forms; this gives him support to endure what opponents say.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r8.anchor: أي أقبل على شأنك من الدعوة إلى الله وذكر الله بأنواع الذكر . وهذا إرشاد إلى ما فيه عون له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r10.claim: Remembrance includes the prayers, as the command to pray at the day's two ends and early night calls prayer remembrance in 11:114–115.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r10.anchor: ويدخل في ذكر الله الصلوات مثل قوله { وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r11.claim: It also includes prophetic supererogatory devotions; the command to remember is a general request encompassing both obligatory and optional acts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p404/r11.anchor: وكذلك النوافل التي هي من خصائص النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بين مفروض منها وغير مفروض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p441#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p441#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p441#2/r1.claim: The night prostration refers to Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p441#2/r1.anchor: ومن الليل فاسجد له يعني المغرب والعشاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p441#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p441#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p441#2/r2.claim: This means night prayer: it was obligatory for the Prophet and voluntary for his community.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p441#2/r2.anchor: وهي صلاة الليل كانت فريضة عليه وهي لأمته تطوع

NASAFI-FULL:v4p306/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p306/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p306/r1.claim: Pray the two evening prayers, Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ, during part of the night.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p306/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p306/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p306/r2.claim: Perform tahajjud for a long portion of the night: two-thirds, half, or one-third.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p306/r2.anchor: أى تهجد له طريق طويلة من الليل ثلثيه أو نصفه أو ثلثه
